summary:
AstroCare is an AI-powered, offline-first health monitoring platform designed to support astronaut safety during long-duration space missions. Astronauts face serious health risks, including radiation exposure, sleep disturbances, cardiovascular changes, and communication delays with Earth.

Our team developed AstroCare to help astronauts monitor their health independently and identify unusual changes early. The platform uses simulated wearable sensor data to track vital signs, compare measurements with personal health baselines, and generate explainable alerts using machine learning.

AstroCare also includes cognitive performance testing, exercise tracking, medical supply management, automated health reports, and Nova, an evidence-based AI assistant.

Using real research datasets from PhysioNet and NASA, the project demonstrates how intelligent, offline-capable technology could support crew health monitoring during missions to the Moon and Mars.

AstroCare is a research prototype, not a clinically validated medical device.
details:
AstroCare is an intelligent health monitoring platform designed to address the medical challenges of long-duration space exploration.

How It Works:

The system uses simulated wearable sensor data to monitor astronauts' heart rate, blood pressure, temperature, sleep, and physical activity. Machine learning models analyze these measurements against individual baselines and expected ranges to identify unusual changes.

Key Features:

  • Continuous vital-sign monitoring and automated alerts
  • Personalized health baselines and trend analysis
  • AI-assisted health monitoring using machine learning
  • Nova, a source-citing medical knowledge assistant
  • Cognitive performance and fatigue assessment
  • Exercise and medical supply tracking
  • Automated health summaries and emergency handovers
  • Offline functionality for missions with communication delays
  • NASA spaceflight biomarker visualization and radiation planning

Technologies Used:

React, TypeScript, Material UI, Python, scikit-learn, machine learning, IndexedDB, and an optional FastAPI/SQLite backend.

Innovation and Impact:

Unlike systems that rely only on fixed health thresholds, AstroCare considers each astronaut's personal baseline and identifies gradual changes over time. Its offline-first design supports independent crew monitoring when communication with Earth is delayed.

The project uses NASA spaceflight resources and publicly available medical datasets to demonstrate a potential approach to astronaut health monitoring.

Limitations:

AstroCare uses simulated crew data. Its models are trained on Earth-based medical datasets and would require astronaut-specific validation before operational use. It does not diagnose conditions or replace professional medical judgment.
